claims.episode_span: set to reach government accounts on Tuesday or Wednesday

claims.supporting_quote: Bolivia's Finance Ministry confirmed Monday that $214 million from the International Monetary Fund was set to reach government accounts on Tuesday or Wednesday — the opening tranche of a $1.9 billion package that marks La Paz's return to multi-year IMF financing for the first time in two decades.

claims.claim: Further IMF disbursements depend on benchmarks including zero central-bank financing of the deficit, and the program is expected to catalyze about 4 billion dollars more.
claims.episode_span: expected to catalyze about 4 billion dollars more

claims.supporting_quote: The program — Bolivia's first multi-year IMF arrangement since 2006 — is expected to catalyze around $4 billion in additional multilateral financing, bringing potential total external support to roughly $5.9 billion over three years.
